title: OSHA construction excavations practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction excavations practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P it comes from.

questions.question: Forms are built inside a wide excavation. When does Subpart P say the excavation is also considered a trench?

options.A: When the forms are taller than 5 feet
options.B: When the forms reduce the dimension from the forms to the side of the excavation to 15 feet or less, measured at the bottom
options.C: Only when the excavation is deeper than 20 feet
options.D: Never; only the original width decides it

questions.explanation: "If forms or other structures are installed or constructed in an excavation so as to reduce the dimension measured from the forms or structure to the side of the excavation to 15 feet (4.6 m) or less (measured at the bottom of the excavation), the excavation is also considered to be a trench."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.650, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Apart from approving manufactured protective systems or tabulated data for interstate commerce, in which state must a "registered professional engineer" under Subpart P be registered?

options.A: The state where the employer has its head office
options.B: The state where the engineer lives
options.C: Any state at all
options.D: The state where the work is to be performed

questions.explanation: A registered professional engineer "means a person who is registered as a professional engineer in the state where the work is to be performed." Registration in any state counts only for those interstate design approvals.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.650, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who must design a structural ramp used for access or egress of equipment in an excavation?

options.A: A competent person qualified in structural design
options.B: The equipment operator
options.C: Any laborer on the crew
options.D: The utility company

questions.explanation: "Structural ramps used for access or egress of equipment shall be designed by a competent person qualified in structural design, and shall be constructed in accordance with the design."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A ramp into an excavation is built from two or more structural members. What does Subpart P require of those members?

options.A: They must be painted a high-visibility color
options.B: They must be spaced at least 1 inch apart
options.C: They must be connected together to prevent displacement
options.D: They must be laid loose so they can be moved quickly

questions.explanation: "Ramps and runways constructed of two or more structural members shall have the structural members connected together to prevent displacement."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long does Subpart P give utility companies or owners to respond to a request to locate underground utility installations (unless state or local law requires longer) before the employer may proceed with caution using detection equipment?

options.A: 2 hours
options.B: 8 hours
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 72 hours

questions.explanation: When utilities "cannot respond to a request to locate underground utility installations within 24 hours (unless a longer period is required by state or local law)," the employer may proceed with caution, using detection equipment or other acceptable means.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Water, adjacent structures and falling material
questions.question: When may an excavation undermine a sidewalk or pavement?

options.A: Only when a support system or another method of protection protects employees from the possible collapse of such structures
options.B: Whenever no vehicles are parked on it
options.C: Whenever the excavation is less than 4 feet deep
options.D: Whenever the work will be finished the same day

questions.explanation: "Sidewalks, pavements, and appurtenant structure shall not be undermined unless a support system or another method of protection is provided to protect employees from the possible collapse of such structures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Ventilation is being used to bring atmospheric contaminants in an excavation down to acceptable levels. How often must the atmosphere be tested?

options.A: Once, at the start of the job
options.B: Once a week
options.C: Only when someone notices an odor
options.D: As often as necessary to ensure that the atmosphere remains safe

questions.explanation: "When controls are used that are intended to reduce the level of atmospheric contaminants to acceptable levels, testing shall be conducted as often as necessary to ensure that the atmosphere remains safe."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Hazardous atmospheric conditions may reasonably be expected to develop in an excavation. Which of these is listed as emergency rescue equipment that must be readily available?

options.A: A portable fire extinguisher only
options.B: Breathing apparatus, a safety harness and line, or a basket stretcher
options.C: A first aid kit only
options.D: A two-way radio only

questions.explanation: "Emergency rescue equipment, such as breathing apparatus, a safety harness and line, or a basket stretcher, shall be readily available where hazardous atmospheric conditions exist or may reasonably be expected to develop during work in an excavation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What limit does Subpart P set, as a share of the gas's lower flammable limit, above which precautions such as ventilation must prevent employee exposure to a flammable gas?

options.A: 20 percent
options.B: 5 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 100 percent

questions.explanation: Precautions must prevent exposure to "a concentration of a flammable gas in excess of 20 percent of the lower flammable limit of the gas."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee entering a bell-bottom pier hole wears a harness with a lifeline. What does Subpart P require of that lifeline?

options.A: It may double as the line used to handle materials
options.B: It needs attending only while the employee enters and exits
options.C: It must be separate from any material-handling line and individually attended at all times
options.D: It is needed only when the hole is deeper than 20 feet

questions.explanation: "The lifeline shall be separate from any line used to handle materials, and shall be individually attended at all times while the employee wearing the lifeline is in the excavation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Water, adjacent structures and falling material
questions.question: When water removal equipment is used to control water in an excavation, who must monitor the equipment and operations?

options.A: The utility company
options.B: A competent person
options.C: A registered professional engineer
options.D: The local fire department

questions.explanation: "The water removal equipment and operations shall be monitored by a competent person to ensure proper operation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Subpart P requires daily inspections of excavations by a competent person. In what circumstance does it say those inspections are required?

options.A: Only for excavations deeper than 20 feet
options.B: Only when OSHA requests one
options.C: Only for excavations open longer than a week
options.D: Only when employee exposure can be reasonably anticipated

questions.explanation: "These inspections are only required when employee exposure can be reasonably anticipated."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When the competent person finds evidence of a situation that could result in a possible cave-in, what does Subpart P require?

options.A: Employees keep working while the competent person watches the face
options.B: The employer files a report with OSHA within 24 hours
options.C: The employer posts a warning sign at the edge
options.D: Exposed employees are removed from the hazardous area until the necessary precautions have been taken

questions.explanation: In that case "exposed employees shall be removed from the hazardous area until the necessary precautions have been taken to ensure their safety."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.651, Specific excavation requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In a trench, material may be excavated up to 2 feet below the bottom of the members of a support system only if what is true?

options.A: The trench is less than 10 feet deep
options.B: The system is designed to resist the forces calculated for the full depth of the trench, and there are no indications of a possible loss of soil from behind or below the bottom of the support system
options.C: A competent person is present at the trench
options.D: The soil has been classified as Type C

questions.explanation: This is permitted "only if the system is designed to resist the forces calculated for the full depth of the trench, and there are no indications while the trench is open of a possible loss of soil from behind or below the bottom of the support system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may employees work on the face of a sloped or benched excavation at a level above other employees?

options.A: Whenever the upper employees work slowly
options.B: Whenever they are within 25 feet of a ladder
options.C: Only when the employees at the lower levels are adequately protected from falling, rolling, or sliding material or equipment
options.D: Whenever the benches are less than 4 feet high

questions.explanation: "Employees shall not be permitted to work on the faces of sloped or benched excavations at levels above other employees except when employees at the lower levels are adequately protected from the hazard of falling, rolling, or sliding material or equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who must approve a sloping or benching system that does not use Option (1), (2) or (3)?

options.A: A registered professional engineer
options.B: The equipment operator
options.C: The utility company
options.D: The property owner

questions.explanation: Such systems "shall be approved by a registered professional engineer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must the removal of a support system begin?

options.A: At the top of the excavation
options.B: At the bottom of the excavation
options.C: At the end nearest the spoil pile
options.D: At the middle of the trench

questions.explanation: "Removal shall begin at, and progress from, the bottom of the excavation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Employees are not allowed inside a shield while the shield is being what?

options.A: Installed, removed, or moved vertically
options.B: Inspected by the competent person
options.C: Used in Type A soil
options.D: Used in a trench less than 8 feet deep

questions.explanation: "Employees shall not be allowed in shields when shields are being installed, removed, or moved vertically."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.652, Requirements for protective systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Soil classification and sloping (Appendices A and B)
questions.question: After a soil deposit has been classified, the conditions affecting its classification change. What does Appendix A require?

options.A: The original classification stays for the life of the job
options.B: The deposit is re-tested once a year
options.C: A registered professional engineer must redesign every protective system on site
options.D: A competent person evaluates the changes, and the deposit is reclassified as necessary

questions.explanation: "If, after classifying a deposit, the properties, factors, or conditions affecting its classification change in any way, the changes shall be evaluated by a competent person. The deposit shall be reclassified as necessary to reflect the changed circumstances."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR Part 1926, Subpart P, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Soil classification and sloping (Appendices A and B)
questions.question: During sloping work, small pebbles and clumps keep suddenly separating from the excavation face and trickling down. How does Appendix B treat this?

options.A: As normal settling that needs no action
options.B: As proof that the soil is Type A
options.C: As ravelling, a sign of distress, so the actual slope must be less steep than the maximum allowable slope
options.D: As a sign of dry soil, which allows a steeper slope

questions.explanation: "Distress means that the soil is in a condition where a cave-in is imminent or is likely to occur," and it includes ravelling. "The actual slope shall be less steep than the maximum allowable slope, when there are signs of distress."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR Part 1926, Subpart P, Appendix B (as of Nov 3, 2026)
